answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small deposit and build a reputation trail over time, so spawning many fake accounts costs real resources. Like a dune that shifts yet keeps its shape, the network filters newcomers through a narrow ledge of gradual trust, while a prism of independent attestations — peers, tasks completed, and stake history — splits one claimed identity into verifiable signals, so sybil clusters stand out as identical low-cost copies.
